data.title: H&R REIT breakup plan falls short in unitholder vote
data.description:
Canada's H&R Real Estate Investment Trust said on Friday its unitholders voted against a previously announced C$6.7 billion ($4.7 billion) breakup deal.

The deal, announced in August, was meant to close a multi-year effort to simplify H&R's portfolio and sharpen its focus on residential real estate.

  • H&R had agreed to the breakup deal, under which GO Residential REIT was to acquire its residential portfolio in the US, while a group including Blackstone and entities tied to H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter would buy the other assets

  • Unitholders rejected the deal at a special meeting on Friday, prompting H&R to terminate the arrangement with immediate effect

  • GO Residential said on Friday it would seek a termination fee of C$102.13 million ($71.65 million), adding it was "disappointed" by the meeting's outcome

  • No termination fee would be payable to the consortium, H&R said

  • H&R will also back away from a proposed purchase of a 70% interest in two joint venture development properties owned by Lantower Residential Real Estate Development Trust that it announced in October

  • The company plans to reinstate monthly distributions, pursue asset sales and begin a board rejig that would include CEO succession planning

data.title: Vail Resorts and 3 More Stocks See Action From Activist Investors — Barrons.com
data.description:
These disclosures are from 13Ds filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 13Ds are filed within 10 days of an entity's attaining more than 5% in any class of a company's securities. Subsequent changes in holdings or intentions must be reported in amended filings. This material is from Nov. 5 through Nov. 11, 2026. Source: VerityData

Activist Filings

Vail Resorts (MTN) DKR Oasis Management raised its stake in the mountain resort operator to 3,429,033 shares. Oasis did so through the purchase of 207,858 Vail Resorts shares from Sept. 29 through Oct. 9 at per share prices ranging from $135.10 to $146.

On Oct. 30, Oasis withdrew its nominations of Bryce Roberts and retired Olympic athlete Picabo Street, narrowing its slate of director nominees to former Walt Disney CEO Robert Chapek and M. Ashton Hudson. In a Nov. 2 letter urging shareholders to elect the pair, Oasis pointed to a more than 50% decline in the share price over the past five years, a 15% drop in North American skier visits last season against an industry decline of 10%, and roughly 12% lower pass unit sales for the upcoming season.

Oasis also outlined initiatives including new pass and ticket offerings, better food and beverage value, expanded year-round use of the company's mountains, modernized marketing, a stronger loyalty program, and upgraded technology.

Following the latest purchases, Oasis owns a 9.6% stake in Vail Resorts' outstanding stock. Shares of Vail Resorts have gained roughly 15.3% in value in 2026.

Increases in Holdings

Metalla Royalty (MTA) Tether Holdings raised its stake in the precious-metals royalty and streaming company to 13,663,050 shares. Tether Holdings did so through the purchase of 453,874 Metalla Royalty shares from Oct. 26 through Nov. 4 at per share prices ranging from $7.20 to $7.73. Following the latest purchases, Tether Holdings owns a 14.6% stake in Metalla Royalty's outstanding stock. Shares of Metalla Royalty have remained mostly flat in 2026.

Decreases in Holdings

Vir Biotechnology (VIR) ARCH Venture Partners lowered its stake in the clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company to 12,508,029 shares. ARCH Venture Partners did so through the sale of 796,175 Vir Biotechnology shares from Nov. 3 through Nov. 5 at per share prices ranging from $10.98 to $12.16. Following the latest sales, ARCH Venture Partners continues to own a 7.3% stake in Vir Biotechnology's outstanding stock. Shares of Vir Biotechnology have gained roughly 121% in value in 2026.

Metropolitan Bank Holding (MCB) Patriot Financial Partners lowered its stake in the commercial bank holding company to 584,946 shares. Patriot Financial Partners did so through the sale of 79,938 Metropolitan Bank Holding shares from Oct. 27 through Nov. 5 at per share prices ranging from $98 to $98.10. Following the latest sales, Patriot Financial Partners continues to own a 4.8% stake in Metropolitan Bank Holding's outstanding stock, placing Patriot Financial Partners below the 5% threshold that would require it to report further sales. Shares of Metropolitan Bank Holding have gained approximately 25.4% in value in 2026.

data.title: Wheat Futures Recover on Russia-Ukraine Strife — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery rose 1.5% on the Chicago Board of Trade Friday to $5.93 1/4 a bushel as Russia and Ukraine continue strikes after this week's talks failed to produce an agreement to ease Black Sea tensions.
  • Soybeans for January delivery rose 1% to $12.31 1/2 a bushel.
  • Corn for December delivery rose 0.7% to $4.45 1/2 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Bouncing Back: Wheat futures rebound back from the previous day's losses as Russia and Ukraine step up strikes, with no deal seen to ease Black Sea shipping. Brazil cut its 2026 wheat production estimate to 5.3 million metric tons from 5.7 million tons, while Argentina's Rosario exchange raised its wheat forecast for the country to 24.3 million tons from 23.8 million tons.

Mixed Export Sales: The USDA reported corn export sales of 3.48 million metric tons for last week, including a marketing-year high 2.88 million tons for 2026/27 and 594,400 tons for 2027/28. Soybean sales fell 21% from the week before to 1.15 million tons for 2026/27, with an additional 11,200 tons sold for 2027/28. Wheat export sales fell 66% from the previous week to 182,800 tons, a marketing-year low.

Flash Sales: Private exporters reported sales of 303,300 metric tons of corn to Mexico--272,820 tons for the 2026/27 marketing year and 30,480 tons for 2027/28, the USDA said. In addition, soybean sales for 2026/27 included 134,000 tons to China, 120,000 tons to Vietnam and 100,000 tons to unknown destinations

INSIGHT

More Please: Last week's U.S. corn export sales, equivalent to 113.4 million bushels for 2026/27, were the largest for any week since January and the most on record for the comparable week, said Mike Castle of StoneX. "These are the kind of weeks corn bulls need to see help the weak 2026/27 cumulative sales pace play catch-up." Export sales are still lagging last year by 27.8%, Castle added in a note.

Steady Outlook: Brazilian national supply company Conab held its estimate for the 2026/27 soybean harvest at 181.6 million metric tons, with planting 66.8% complete as of the first week of November. Initial development has been generally positive, but conditions have varied across regions, the state company said. "Irregular rainfall, combined with high temperatures and the effects of the El Niño phenomenon at the start of this cycle, calls for a cautious outlook regarding productive potential." Conab sees corn production from its three harvests reaching 148 million tons, also unchanged from October, with higher planted area compared with last year partially offset by lower yields.

AHEAD

  • Tyson Foods Inc. will release its 4Q 2026 earnings report before the market opens Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.
  • The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10"30 a.m. Wednesday

Write to Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: Two-year yields headed for biggest weekly jump in two years
data.description:
Key points:
  • Two-year yields headed for largest weekly gain in two years
  • Traders expect faster pace of rate hikes due to elevated inflation
  • October producer price gains below economists' expectations

By Karen Brettell

Interest rate-sensitive 2-year Treasury yields are headed for the largest weekly increase in more than two years on Friday, after hotter-than-expected consumer price inflation and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary this week led traders to ramp up bets on faster interest rate increases.

Treasury yields briefly dipped on Friday after data showed that producer price inflation was lower than economists expected in October, though it showed the largest annual gain in four years.

Yields remain sharply higher on the week as traders see rising odds that the US central bank could hike rates by a larger-than-usual 50 basis points in December, or raise rates by 25 basis points at each of the next three meetings.

“Inflation is stubbornly high and the Fed's going to need to act a little bit quicker and a little bit more aggressively,” said Molly Brooks, US rates strategist at TD Securities.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point hike at the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting, compared with zero probability a week ago, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch Tool.

The odds of the Fed hiking rates by a cumulative 50 basis points by January have risen to 67%, from 16% a week ago, while 75 basis points of hikes by March has a 48% chance, up from 6% a week ago.

The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield was last up 0.34 basis point at 4.867%. It earlier reached 4.892%, the highest since October 14, and is headed for the biggest weekly increase since the first week of October 2024.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 4.64 basis points to 5.149%. It reached 5.174%, the highest since October 14, and is on track for its biggest weekly rise since the April 2025 "tariff tantrum."

The closely watched yield curve between 2- and 10-year notes (US2US10=TWEB) steepened to 28 basis points. It reached 21 basis points on Thursday, the flattest level since September 24.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller raised the prospect of a larger-than-usual 50-basis-point hike in December when he said on Tuesday that the central bank should consider a half-point increase if the inflation picture worsens.

A heavy slate of Fed speakers since then has also bolstered the case that a faster pace of rate hikes may be needed to stem inflation, which has been running above the Fed’s 2% annual target for almost six years.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Friday that tighter monetary policy is coming because of high inflation, in comments that suggested the US central bank may have to raise interest rates more than she initially expected.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that her "bias" is that the central bank will need to increase its policy rate, particularly with services inflation moving in the wrong direction and some signs of inflation persistence.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said that price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices, contradicting comments by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that the Fed should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war.

Concerns about the ongoing war with Iran have added to the move higher in rates. US President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US did not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus "his complete and total attention" on what Trump said were crime and corruption in Democratic-led cities and states.
